citation.title: Active spectroscopy measurements of the deuterium temperature, rotation, and density from the core to scrape off layer on the DIII-D tokamak
citation.authors: S. R. Haskey, B. A. Grierson, L. Stagner, C. Chrystal, A. Ashourvan, A. Bortolon, M. D. Boyer, K. H. Burrell, C. Collins, R. J. Groebner, D. H. Kaplan, N. A. Pablant
citation.year: 2018 (manuscript dated 5 June 2018; published in the proceedings of the 22nd HTPD conference)
citation.venue: Unknown from supplied text; likely Review of Scientific Instruments, not verified

topic: Main-ion (deuterium) CER on DIII-D, compared with carbon-impurity CER. Covers spectral fitting, time-slice subtraction, FIDA treatment, and iterative collisional-radiative corrections.
own_question: How can D+ temperature, rotation and density be measured from the core to the scrape-off layer, and what analysis is required to do so?
actual_method_and_evidence: Uses a 32-chord MICER system. Spectra are fit with a C-language fitter (MICEFIT), and apparent values are corrected iteratively with FIDASIM. The paper tests sensitivity to the choice of passive time slice and to including FIDA, and compares D+ with C-VI profiles for an Ohmic case and an ITER baseline case. The evidence comes from a few example discharges and is offline only.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Conventional CER temperature on DIII-D comes from carbon-impurity C-VI emission. Main-ion and impurity rotation can differ substantially near the edge, so CES impurity labels are not main-ion truth.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p1 Introduction; p7 Sec IV, Figs 7-8
claim_checks.qualification: Shown for DIII-D example discharges. In Fig 7 the carbon and deuterium temperatures were near identical, so the difference is demonstrated for rotation, not for Ti generally.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Charge-exchange analysis is offline and computationally heavy. Faster spectral fitting enabled between-shot fitting, but the atomic-physics iterations remained slow.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p3 Sec III A-III; p5 Sec III C; p8 Conclusions
claim_checks.qualification: This applies to MICER on DIII-D, not to KSTAR CES. Between-shot fitting is not real-time operation.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Typical integration time is 5 ms, with beam blips used for beam-on/beam-off subtraction. In the Ohmic case, measurements come every 400 ms. No report-arrival latency is given.
validation_if_relevant: No ML validation is involved; the paper reports consistency checks across passive time-slice choices only.
forbidden_inferences: Do not use it as evidence about KSTAR CES latency.
It does not show that impurity temperature is wrong in general.
It does not support BES/ECEI nowcasting.
Do not describe it as real-time deployment.
Do not equate main-ion Ti with our carbon labels.
Do not take the DOI from the reference list.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background establishing that our labels are impurity CES measurements rather than main-ion truth, and that CES analysis is cadence- and compute-limited. Cite it briefly.
